title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. Every market price is an implicit forecast of future cash flows.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett / Michael Mauboussin

web_blocks.html: On November 16, 2026, Coforge closed at ₹2,010.00 on the NSE, giving it a market cap of ₹89,051.21 Cr [24]. On trailing twelve-month (TTM) numbers through Q2 FY27, the stock trades at 40.06x TTM P/E and 4.04x Price-to-Book [1, 24]. TTM revenue grew 41.21% YoY and TTM EPS rose 47.37% YoY [24]. A 40x trailing multiple looks high beside legacy IT firms, yet backward earnings understate the merged scale. In Q2 FY27 alone, Coforge + Encora printed ₹6,170.8 Cr in revenue (~₹24,683 Cr annualized) [5]. Management also raised FY27 EBIT margin guidance to 16.0%, targeting 17.0% by Q4 FY27, backed by a $2.38 billion 12-month order book (+45% YoY) [5].

Does ₹2,010.00 offer real upside, or does it price perfection? We test this two ways. First, a Reverse DCF strips away stories and solves for the 10-year free cash flow growth rate baked into ₹89,051 Cr. Second, a Peer Snapshot Table compares Coforge directly against Persistent Systems, L&T Technology Services, KPIT Technologies, and Mphasis [24, 25, 26, 27, 28].

web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹2,010, the market embeds ~15.8% 10-year FCF CAGR at an 11.5% discount rate—demanding, but achievable if Encora G&A synergies (20–25% reduction) and 16.5%+ EBIT margins convert into cash and pay down the ₹6,026 Cr debt load.

web_blocks.title: Why the Persistent Discount Exists—and How It Closes
paragraphs: Persistent Systems trades at 51.75x TTM P/E because its growth is organic, asset-light, and net-cash [25]. Coforge absorbed ~20% equity dilution and ₹6,026 Cr in debt to close Encora in May 2026 [1, 6]. That lifted intangibles and pulled headline ROE down to 13.46% [24].

Coforge has already run this playbook at SLK Global and Cigniti [2, 8]. If Encora resumes organic growth in Q3 FY27, G&A costs drop 20%–25%, and DSO improves toward 75 days, FY28E EPS can reach ₹78–₹82 [5, 7]. ROE would recover above 18%, closing part of the multiple gap.

web_blocks.html: Historical bands support this view. Over five years, Coforge has traded between 24x (during the 2022–23 tech pause) and 55x (at the 2021 peak), with a median near 38x–40x [1]. At 40.06x TTM P/E—roughly 25.5x–26.5x annualized H2 FY27E earnings—the stock sits at its median multiple while order-book scale ($2.38B) and margins (16.0%–17.0%) are rising [5, 24].

Valuation Trigger: What would change our ₹2,620 Base valuation? A Q3 or Q4 FY27 print showing Encora revenue shrinking QoQ, EBIT margin slipping below 15.0%, or debtor days staying above 88 days would cut FY28E EPS toward ₹62 and force a bear-case de-rating toward 26x (₹1,620).

book_paragraphs: Now you and I step out of the price-blind room and look at the ticker tape. As of the November 16, 2026 close on the NSE, Coforge trades at ₹2,010.00, giving the combined Coforge-Encora enterprise a market capitalization of ₹89,051.21 Cr. At first glance, a trailing twelve-month P/E of 40.06x and Price-to-Book of 4.04x might make a traditional value investor flinch. Why would anyone pay forty times trailing earnings for an IT services company when legacy giants trade in the mid-twenties?

The answer lies in what trailing earnings conceal. Trailing twelve-month numbers blend pre-Encora quarters with just one full quarter of the combined platform. In Q2 FY27 alone, Coforge generated ₹6,170.8 Cr in revenue—an annualized run rate approaching ₹24,700 Cr—while raising its full-year FY27 EBIT margin guidance to 16.0% and laying out a roadmap to 17.0% by Q4 FY27. More importantly, its 12-month executable order book hit $2.38 billion, up 45% year-over-year, backed by over $1 billion in quarterly order intake across eight large deal wins.

Rather than guessing whether 40x is cheap or expensive, let us invert the problem using a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow model. At ₹2,010 per share and roughly ₹93,851 Cr of enterprise value (factoring in post-Encora net debt), what is the market already pricing in? Using an 11.5% cost of capital and a 5.0% terminal growth rate, today's share price implies roughly a 15.8% compound annual growth rate in free cash flow over the next decade. That is not a layup, nor is it fantasy. It requires Coforge to hold 12% to 15% organic top-line growth, sustain 16% to 17% operating margins, and convert roughly 80% of net profit into free cash flow as Encora's legal-entity rationalization finishes and working capital normalizes.

When we line Coforge up against its four closest Indian peers on the exact same November 16, 2026 snapshot, the relative pricing becomes even clearer. Persistent Systems—the market's darling in digital engineering—trades at 51.75x TTM P/E at ₹5,911. L&T Technology Services trades at 29.02x at ₹4,208, KPIT Technologies at 27.26x at ₹531.65, and Mphasis at 23.34x at ₹2,445. Coforge sits at 40.06x, a nearly 23% valuation discount to Persistent despite posting 41.21% YoY TTM revenue growth and 47.37% YoY TTM EPS growth.

Why does that 11-turn discount to Persistent exist? Two honest reasons. First, Persistent grew organically with a clean, net-cash balance sheet. Coforge used equity dilution and ₹6,026 Cr of debt to swallow Encora, temporarily depressing headline ROE to 13.46% on the expanded equity base. Second, investors want proof that Encora's flat Q2 quarter-on-quarter revenue was truly caused by contract novations and US-to-India entity migrations rather than underlying demand softness. If Q3 and Q4 FY27 confirm that Encora resumes growing alongside core Coforge while G&A synergies knock 20% to 25% off overhead costs, that valuation gap has room to narrow even as earnings compound toward ₹78–₹82 per share by FY28E.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Paying for Integration Execution
book_callouts.text: You are not buying a sleepy, debt-free dividend payer here. At 40x trailing earnings and 15.8% implied FCF growth, you are underwriting Sudhir Singh's ability to repeat the SLK Global and Cigniti playbook at four times the scale. If DSO stays stuck near 88 days and Encora stalls, the multiple compresses toward 26x (₹1,620). If synergies land and cash flows pay down debt, ₹2,620 over 18–24 months is simply 32.8x FY28E earnings.

book_subsections.title: Deconstructing the 15.8% Implied FCF Hurdle
paragraphs: Every great investment error happens when an analyst mistakes a good company for a cheap stock without checking what expectations are already baked into the price. At ₹89,051 Cr of market cap, Coforge is no longer an undiscovered mid-cap. It is an institutional heavyweight where every basis point of margin and every day of receivable collection is scrutinized by global funds.

To clear a 15.8% 10-year FCF CAGR hurdle, Coforge has two distinct levers. The first is revenue scale: the $2.38 billion executable order book covers nearly 85% of next-twelve-month consensus revenue, giving rare visibility in an uncertain US macro environment. The second is cash conversion: in FY26, CFO-to-EBITDA moderated to 76% as debtor days stretched to 88. Simply restoring CFO-to-PAT toward 85% and retiring ₹1,500–₹2,000 Cr of debt annually out of free cash flow transfers enterprise value directly from debtholders back to equity shareholders.

book_subsections.title: Peer Multiples: Why Quality Diverges Within Mid-Tier IT
paragraphs: Investors often lump mid-tier Indian IT firms into a single basket, which is a mistake. KPIT Technologies (27.26x) and LTTS (29.02x) are heavily tethered to global automotive and industrial R&D budgets, which face cyclical capex pauses in Europe and Detroit. Mphasis (23.34x) has struggled with mortgage-rate sensitivity and slower top-line momentum. Coforge and Persistent stand apart because they sit at the intersection of banking/financial services modernization, travel/hospitality platforms, and cloud/AI data engineering—verticals where clients are actively funding multi-year cost-takeout and platform-modernization deals.

At 40.06x TTM P/E, Coforge is priced right near its own five-year median multiple while delivering peak order-book velocity. That combination—median multiple, accelerating fundamentals—is rare, provided the post-Encora balance sheet deleverages on schedule.

book_subsections.title: Sensitivity Check: What Happens If Encora Synergies Slip by 100 bps?
paragraphs: Let us stress-test our Reverse DCF before moving to the chart. Suppose Encora's G&A cost-reduction program delivers only half of its targeted 20% to 25% savings, capping consolidated FY28E EBIT margin at 15.0% instead of 16.5%, while debtor days remain stuck at 88. In that scenario, FY28E EPS would likely land closer to ₹68–₹70 rather than ₹80, and the market would likely re-rate the stock down toward 26x–28x forward earnings—roughly ₹1,770 to ₹1,960, or flat-to-negative returns from CMP ₹2,010.

Conversely, if Coforge hits its stated 17.0% EBIT margin exit rate by Q4 FY27 and Encora grows at 12%+ alongside core Coforge, FY28E EPS can exceed ₹84. At 35x forward earnings—still a sharp discount to Persistent's current 51.75x trailing multiple—the stock supports our ₹2,950 Bull target. That asymmetric sensitivity is why monitoring quarterly EBIT margin and DSO is non-negotiable.

book_subsections.title: Historical Valuation Bands: Why 40x TTM Today Differs from 2021
paragraphs: At the peak of the 2021 post-COVID digital bubble, Indian mid-tier IT stocks traded at 50x to 65x earnings on temporary stimulus-fueled demand and zero-percent interest rates. When rates normalized in 2022, multiples compressed sharply toward 24x–28x.

Today's 40.06x trailing multiple at ₹2,010.00 sits in a very different regime. First, it is anchored right near Coforge's five-year median valuation rather than a cyclical peak. Second, trailing earnings still understate full-year combined Coforge + Encora profitability, putting the stock closer to 25.5x–26.5x annualized H2 FY27E run-rate earnings. That provides a far sturdier valuation floor as long as Q3 and Q4 FY27 execution stays on track.
